sources.title: Braids: A Survey
sources.publication_or_version: Handbook of Knot Theory author manuscript dated 2004-12-02
useful_locators: Section 2.2 and Lemmas 2.1-2.2, printed pp. 13-17: Yamada-Vogel reducing algorithm and Alexander theorem
Section 2.3 and Lemmas 2.3-2.8, printed pp. 17-26: Markov theorem proof, with the four-band terminal move referred to Traczyk for details
Section 4.2, printed p. 47: reduced-Burau determinant formula for the one-variable Alexander polynomial
Section 4.4, printed pp. 52-53: topological reduced-Burau construction from the infinite cyclic cover of a punctured disk
Theorem 3, printed p. 17: Reidemeister theorem is cited, not proved in this source
limitations: Braid survey, not a general knot-group or peripheral-system treatment
Some Markov and representation subarguments cite other papers
Its 2004 open-problem statements are not current 2026 status evidence

sources.title: Burau Maps and Twisted Alexander Polynomials
sources.publication_or_version: arXiv:1510.06678v2, 2016-08-03; submitted to Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society
useful_locators: Section 2(b), printed pp. 5-7: twisted cellular homology and the braid action
Section 2(c)-(d), printed pp. 7-11: based-chain torsion, twisted link torsion, Fox derivatives and Wada quotient
Lemma 2.6, printed p. 8: torsion of H1 implies acyclicity over Q(H) under the stated link-exterior conditions
Proposition 3.4, printed p. 12: twisted Burau matrix entries are evaluated Fox derivatives
Theorem 3.15 and proof, printed pp. 16-17: colored twisted-Burau determinant formula by adding the axis and applying a torsion product formula
limitations: The Wada quotient equals twisted torsion by citation to Kitano/Wada; the general equality and its invariance are not proved in this paper
Coefficient ring R is commutative and H is free abelian; this is not a noncommutative Alexander-order theorem
The braid theorem assumes the representation extends to the closed-braid complement

sources.title: A Survey of Classical Knot Concordance
sources.coverage: Complete extracted PDF, including references; physical p. 1 is handbook contents and article text begins on printed p. 2
useful_locators: Definitions 2.1-2.5 and Theorem 2.6, printed pp. 4-5: smooth concordance, Seifert pairing and metabolic form; slice-implies-metabolic proof is compressed
Section 3.1, printed p. 7: Levine-Tristram signatures
Section 3.3, printed p. 7: Seifert determinant polynomial and unit ambiguity
Sections 4-5, printed pp. 9-13: Casson-Gordon setup, satellite-companion formula and genus-one applications
Section 6, printed pp. 13-14: locally flat topological concordance and slice-disk double branched-cover discussion
Section 10, printed pp. 20-21: open problems as of 2004 only
limitations: Explicitly excludes link concordance and focuses on classical knots
Smooth and topological locally flat categories are distinguished; do not transfer claims to wild knots
This survey often states imported theorems or proof sketches rather than complete proofs
Its frontier and open-problem status is historical, not current

sources.title: Seifert Forms and Concordance
sources.coverage: Complete published note and references; printed pp. 403-408
useful_locators: Theorem 1.2 and proof, printed pp. 404, 407-408: homology of cyclic branched covers and cyclotomic Alexander factors
Theorem 3.1 and proof, printed pp. 406-407: cyclic branched-cover homology order formula and prime-power rational-homology-sphere corollary
Theorem 1.1 and proof, printed pp. 405-406: band infection and Casson-Gordon signatures produce nonconcordant knots with a fixed Seifert matrix
limitations: Uses Casson-Gordon and branched-cover inputs from other works
The displayed Hermitian signature formula contains a coefficient inconsistency; repair the conjugation convention before reuse
It does not prove general Seifert S-equivalence

sources.title: The Multivariable Alexander Polynomial for a Closed Braid
sources.coverage: Complete paper, including proof and references
useful_locators: Section 2 and Theorem 1, printed pp. 2-4: colored reduced Burau matrix and multivariable polynomial of braid closure together with axis
Remark (2), printed pp. 3-4: Torres-Fox deletion of the axis and knot/link normalization
Proof of Theorem 1, printed pp. 4-6: braid-group presentation, Fox Jacobian, chain rule and determinant calculation
limitations: Specialized to links represented as braid closures, with the axis retained for the determinant formula
Quotes the general Fox invariant and Torres-Fox rule; it does not prove all presentation-invariance foundations

sources.title: Linking Numbers in Rational Homology 3-Spheres, Cyclic Branched Covers and Infinite Cyclic Covers
sources.coverage: Complete paper, including proofs and references
useful_locators: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, printed pp. 5-8: rational surgery-linking matrix formula
Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.3, printed pp. 8-12: Goeritz form invariance and double-branched-cover linking
Proposition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, printed pp. 13-14: Seifert S-equivalence and p-fold branched-cover linking from the block matrix
Lemma 4.6 and Theorem 4.1, printed pp. 16-18: infinite-cyclic-cover linking pairing from the Seifert matrix
limitations: Assumes the relevant auxiliary links have zero/even linking with the branch knot so the required disjoint surface exists
The branched-cover surgery presentation is attributed to Akbulut-Kirby rather than proved here
The p. 2 Hermitian signature matrix has a typographic inconsistency with its stated factorization

sources.title: Notes on Reidemeister Torsion
sources.publication_or_version: PDF text dated 2001-07-28; host catalogue labels the notes 1997
useful_locators: Definitions 4 and 6, printed pp. 3-4: torsion of based acyclic complexes and finite CW spaces
Theorem 15, printed p. 8: internal-basis formula
Example 17, printed pp. 9-10: knot-exterior torsion, deck action, and its relation to the Alexander polynomial
limitations: Introduces ordinary commutative-coefficient R-torsion; it does not develop twisted knot torsion
Its noncommutative discussion is at the Whitehead-torsion level, not a noncommutative Alexander determinant formula
